# RTM RealSim material utilization audit

2026-10-19. Target: Java 8, Forge 1.7.10. This report covers the current working tree, including its pre-existing chemistry, salinity, steelmaking and NEI changes. It is an audit of stock source and registration paths, not a dump of an arbitrary pack's live registry.

## Findings and decisions

The confirmed progression defect is the chromium bootstrap: the ordinary chromite-to-chromium recipe is in the Centrifuge, while the Centrifuge Element requires stainless plate. The new route is **chromite + aluminium powder → ferrochrome + alumina + returned aluminium**, in the existing Chemical Reactor, followed by **6 steel + 2 ferrochrome → 8 stainless**, in the existing Metallurgical Furnace. The existing centrifuge, pure-chromium and foundry routes remain available. A chemical oxide, elemental chromium and ferrochrome are separate identities.

The confirmed lost osmium electronics route was a Soldering Station recipe, introduced in `36b203f25` and removed in `7ee2bec57`: originally one legacy `ingot_osmiridium`, four chips, four capacitors, eight PCBs, rubber and lead wire produced twelve Bismoid Chips; a later revision produced eight Bismoid Boards. Reintroducing that multiplication would conflate contact materials with semiconductor fabrication. The replacement application uses a **separate osmium–iridium contact alloy**, cast through the existing Foundry, in optional batches of Cable Switches. Rhodium has a separate, equally optional contact recipe. These switches retain normal behavior; no durability bonus is claimed.

Most chemical materials already have real intermediate uses after the overhaul. An oxide's reduction, a solvent's recirculation, a coolant's heat transport, a nuclear waste's containment, and a fuel's combustion are legitimate functions. Converting an ingot to nuggets and back, registering an OreDictionary alias, displaying an NEI icon, applying a hazard, or generating a creative subitem does **not** establish a useful sink.

No universal rare-element electronics gate, new machine, technology tier, reactor type, fuel rebalance, ore alias broadening, or reset of persistent identities is introduced. No new use is fabricated for research-only elements, obsolete components or deliberately retained wastes.

## Scope and evidence standard

The inventory below enumerates **211 named material/substitution definitions** (including inline Foundry identities and aliases), **1127 native material/component item fields**, and **243 fluid fields**. These overlapping counts are not counts of elements: `ST`/`SR`, deprecated fluid aliases, compounds, metadata carriers and substitution groups are explicitly distinct cases. Both native fields and metadata families are covered. Decorative/weapon component fields on the material tab are retained in the census so that a broad item-name filter cannot silently hide a material. They do not all require new industrial sinks.

History uses the available HBM-derived pre-RealSim tree immediately before `7ee2bec57`, rather than assuming upstream's newest branch is canonical. “Previous uses” in the tables links its corresponding source locations as a comparison index; line numbers there refer to that historical tree. A historical reference establishes an earlier recipe, not that it was scientifically correct or enabled in every pack.

Historical comparison revision: `5ba5b9455c950fa5cb77fb3b0121192694b11bdd`.
The explicit recipe index follows input/output argument positions for crafting, smelting, assembler, native two-input furnace, centrifuge/shredder maps, soldering, welding and anvil registrations. The process-factory index separately tracks mass-accounted chemistry. Parameterized recipes, enum-driven nuclear consumers, foundry molds, OreDictionary groups, world extraction, fuel acceptance, decay and loot are audited at their native owners below. The tables expose these layers separately instead of pretending a text occurrence proves survival reachability.

The acquisition and use links enumerate explicit registrations; the native-source column additionally includes world/loot/consumer references. A row with no explicit source is **not** certified unobtainable solely on that basis: native acquisition, generated forms and the family decision must also be read. “Unobtainable/Broken” is conservative where stock reachability is unresolved; it does not assert that an external pack cannot supply the material. Runtime NEI interaction, server startup, automation and reload acceptance remain a separate verification layer.

| Classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Functional | A meaningful manufacturing, fuel, construction, chemical or operating role is present. |
| Restored | A lost function or broken progression route is repaired by this change. |
| Expanded | A justified optional application is added. |
| Optional/Specialist | A limited, conditional, nuclear, decorative, fictional or material-form role is intentional. A conversion-only form has no independent terminal sink. |
| Intentionally unused | No defensible additional application is implemented within the existing technology; retain identities for saves/compatibility. |
| Unobtainable/Broken | A stock source or terminal chain remains unresolved or disconnected; no functional claim is made. |

## Registration and execution owners

| Layer | Verified source path and reachability boundary |
|---|---|
| Items, fluids and aliases | `MainRegistry` initializes native items/blocks and OreDictionary identities; `OreDictManager.registerOres` registers ordinary and generated forms. Generation flags alone do not supply sources. `Fluids` assigns persistent numeric identities; aliases are not extra chemical substances. |
| Crafting and smelting | `MainRegistry` → `CraftingManager.mainRegistry` → `AddCraftingRec`, `SmeltingRecipes`, `MineralRecipes`, `RodRecipes`, weapon/tool/armor/powder/consumable registrations. `RegistrationDiagnostics` can reject invalid stacks; stock source paths still require initialized native registrations. |
| Machine defaults/configs | `MainRegistry` → `SerializableRecipe.registerAllHandlers` → `initialize`, which clears each registry, loads an enabled `hbmRecipes/<name>.json` if present, otherwise calls `registerDefaults`, then calls `registerPost`. Custom recipe JSON intentionally overrides defaults. New stock defaults do not bypass an enabled old custom file. |
| Chemistry | `ChemplantRecipes.registerDefaults` selects `ChemistryProcesses.defaults`/factory bills; `ChemRecipe.petroleum` validates physical power/flow and four-port counts, resolves actual items, and binds the paid `ProcessBatch` path. `ProcessMachine` resolves each solid/fluid identity and metadata. Separate native electrolyser, crystallizer, mixer and petroleum loaders remain authoritative for their machines. |
| Foundry | `Mats`/`MatDistribution` resolve actual assays; `CrucibleRecipes` templates select reactions; `TileEntityCrucible` owns heated, quantity-reserved production. `ItemMold.MoldShape` resolves actual OreDictionary outputs. `OreDictManager` registers `ingot_raw:<material ID>` for INGOT autogen. |
| Native furnace | `BlastFurnaceRecipes` is the two-input **Metallurgical Furnace** registry, not the coke-fired multiblock `IndustrialBlastFurnaceRecipes`. `getOutput` and `getInputAmounts` check both quantities and both input orders. Normal and RTG furnace paths use these native counts. |
| Other recipes | `MainRegistry` explicitly registers SILEX, gas centrifuge, anvil, magic and Lemegeton recipes. Magic access is conditional/specialist, not an ordinary early-game guarantee. `PedestalRecipes` and `AmmoPressRecipes` are not added to the stock serializable-handler list. Their definitions are not credited as live stock sinks. |
| Fuels and heat | `SolidFuel`, `FuelSuitability`, `Combustion`, `FuelHandler`, thermal generators and machine-native acceptance tables decide actual suitability. Positive LHV alone never enables a machine. Steam, oxidizers, inert purge and coolants have distinct operating roles. |
| Nuclear states | `RodRecipes`, reactor fuel enums, breeder/outgasser/exposure/fuel-pool/SILEX recipes, `IrradiationLedger` and native reactor code own isotope fabrication, breeding, burnup and waste. Bare ingots, mixed fuel and clad assemblies are not interchangeable. |
| NEI | `NEIConfig`/`NEIRegistry` client registration installs handlers; native crafting uses NEI's crafting view. `CrucibleAlloyingHandler`, `CrucibleCastingHandler`, `CrucibleSmeltingHandler`, `ChemplantRecipeHandler` and native furnace export consume actual production registries. Physical product pages display integer parcels and retained fractional mass. No client-only handler is imported into the new production code. |

## Implemented chains and material accounting

### Chromium bootstrap

1. The stock Excavator bedrock-drop list includes `chunk_chromite` (`MiningConfig`); its construction uses ordinary steel/titanium/copper, motor, tank and Analog Circuit. It does not require stainless or a centrifuge.
2. Tier-2 anvil processing of one chunk produces two chromite parcels. The anvil construction path precedes the Centrifuge.
3. Chemical Reactor template **1201, Chromite Aluminothermic Reduction** accepts **two 1-kg chromite packets and one 1-kg aluminium-powder packet**. The simplified oxide assay is FeCr2O4. The balanced model is `3 FeCr2O4 + 8 Al → 3 FeCr2 + 4 Al2O3`. Real ores contain gangue; this clean process packet does not claim every excavated block is pure laboratory chromite.
4. Per batch, approximately **1.428 kg ferrochrome**, **1.215 kg alumina** and **0.357 kg unused aluminium** are owned outputs. The total is exactly 3 kg on the existing integer mass lattice. Integer items release as available; the saved species-specific mass account retains the rest. Multiple batches accumulate enough ferrochrome for the two-ingot furnace charge. Do not round every batch up to two ingots.
5. The electrically heated reactor pays **4.2 MJ over 20 seconds (210 kW process duty)** plus native cooling. The 1600 C value is the process reference, not a new external-heater requirement. The existing reactor is the repository's electrically heated synthesis/reduction abstraction. The aluminothermic chemistry is exothermic; no usable reaction heat credit is minted. The adopted positive utility bill covers preparation/heating and is a gameplay choice, not a measured industrial energy consumption.
6. Feed **six steel ingots and two ferrochrome ingots** into either native Metallurgical Furnace orientation to obtain **eight stainless ingots**. FeCr2 contains about 65% chromium by mass, giving about **16.25% Cr** in this eight-part charge. This is a ferritic stainless approximation; nickel is not falsely required for every stainless grade.
7. Press or anvil-form stainless plate; the existing Centrifuge Element recipe still requires two stainless plates, titanium, motor and rubber. The new route terminates at that existing component and machine.

The aluminium powder feed uses the existing acquisition/shredding/Bayer routes. It has no stainless-specific dependency. Reactor fabrication uses ordinary steel, copper/tungsten coils, motor, pipes, polymer and Analog Circuit; its cooling uses fresh water. Standard copper/steel manufacture, polymer and Analog Circuit routes remain usable without the Centrifuge. Pack overrides can deliberately alter these dependencies.

The added **Ferrochrome** Foundry ID is **24004**, represented by existing `ingot_raw` metadata. Its process identity `ITEM:ingot_raw@24004` resolves through the established specialist item adapter with exact metadata. It has no `ingotChromium` or `dustChromium` alias. Existing ore grinding, pure Cr refining, Desh and stainless recipes are preserved. The older manganese/selenium-only stainless alternatives remain historical abstractions; their inability to supply chromium is a scientific limitation, not a justification for treating them as the primary bootstrap fix.

### Osmium, iridium and rhodium contacts

The legacy field/OD name `ingot_osmiridium`/`Osmiridium` is displayed as **Osmium** and made from `powder_osmium`. It remains Foundry ID 7699. Reinterpreting all old saves as an alloy would be incorrect.

| Material | Acquisition | Previous uses | Current uses | Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Osmium, legacy Osmiridium identity | Mixed mineral/PGM concentrate → oxidation template 1054 → osmium-tetroxide solution → paid hydrogen reduction 1055 → tiny powder → full powder → Metallurgical Furnace consolidation | Multiplied Bismoid chips/boards in soldering; high-tier anvil and DFC material uses | Existing anvil/DFC uses, now contact-alloy feed | Restored | Recover the contact function through a real alloy, rather than multiplying semiconductor components. |
| Iridium concentrate, oxide and chloride solution | Osmium/Rh residue → oxidation 1057 → carbochlorination 1061 → fluid electrolysis → powder → native Arc Furnace ingot | Specialized electrode/material uses | Existing electrode plus contact-alloy feed | Expanded | Oxide and salt must be reduced/refined; neither directly crafts the alloy. |
| Osmium-Iridium contact alloy | Foundry template **25**: 72 q refined osmium + 72 q refined iridium → **144 q alloy** | New application | Cast ingots for optional Cable Switch manufacturing | Expanded | New persistent ID **24003**; equal Foundry quantities are an adopted gameplay composition, not an asserted weight-percent specification. No wire drawing of this hard/brittle alloy. |
| Rhodium | Rh-bearing concentrate → chlorination 1056 → Rh solution electrolysis → powder → native Arc Furnace ingot | Refining and specialty material states; no need to claim a lost semiconductor function | Optional Cable Switch contacts | Expanded | Pure rhodium is a suitable corrosion-resistant contact material; keep it separate from its chloride solution. |
| Ruthenium | Existing PGM byproducts/RuO2 residue reduction | Upgrade-template and specialist uses | Existing upgrade-template route retained | Optional/Specialist | Existing demand exists. Do not add an unsupported pure-Ru semiconductor recipe or pretend Ru oxide and Ru metal are interchangeable. |

Each contact recipe uses **one alloy ingot OR one rhodium ingot plus eight Coated Red Copper Wires → eight Cable Switches** in a 3×3 crafting grid, with the contact blank in the center. Every switch consumes its own insulated conductor; the contact material supplies multiple machined tips. Existing single-switch lever and mercury recipes remain. Ordinary copper remains the conductor. Existing switch on/off behavior, world saves and network authority remain unchanged. No alternate recipe converts the alloy back to its elements, refunds contacts, or duplicates wire. The specialist route offers an alternative material supply and batch manufacture, not an invented in-game durability statistic.

Only two material identities are added, using existing metadata assets and casting infrastructure; no independent item classes, textures, machines or single-purpose component ladder are needed.

## Historical losses, replacements and deliberate exclusions

| Material/state | Historical change or concern | Current decision |
|---|---|---|
| Osmium/legacy osmiridium | Historical Soldering Station alternative was removed with RealSim electronics. Its chip/board multiplier was not a conservation-respecting contact model. | Restore the defensible contact function through the new alloy and switches. Do not restore raw-material shortcuts into populated boards. |
| Arsenic | An old direct recipe consumer disappears from the simple registration comparison. | GaAs synthesis is now a mass-accounted chemical factory; this is a changed intermediate path, not proof of a dead element. |
| Coltan | Old direct chemical input was moved behind paid leaching/oxide separation. | Coltan → prepared Ta/Nb oxides → reduction remains the appropriate role. Do not restore metal-from-ore shortcuts. |
| Barium | Two earlier direct consumers disappear from the explicit-registry comparison. | Carbonate/oxide/reduction and barium-bearing BBO/optical and radioisotope processes remain state-specific. No compulsory barium on ordinary boards. |
| Vanadium | Earlier direct inputs move to specialist consolidation and inert Desh alloying. | Existing Desh use remains. Erbium returned by consolidation is a recovered process addition, not vanadium creation. |
| Germanium, SmCo, rare-earth metals | Removed bulk-board alternatives must not be inferred to be legitimate because they once existed. | Keep semiconductor preparation, magnets and doped optical crystals distinct from populated circuits; retained actual routes appear in the inventory. |
| Rhodium | Refining without a substantial ordinary terminal consumer. | Add optional electrical contacts. No need for universal catalyst consumption on every chemistry batch. |
| Tennessine; francium; rutherfordium/dubnium samples | Loot/cyclotron or collector identities, no practical workshop material demand. Real superheavy/short-lived elements do not justify bulk engineering recipes. | Intentionally unused industrially; retain samples, acquisition and saved identities. |
| Chinesium989, u238m2 and disconnected novelty forms | Disabled/commented former production or no stock terminal consumer. | Unobtainable/Broken where acquisition is disconnected; retained compatibility assets are not promoted into new progression requirements. |
| PET and Latex identities | Declared names/legacy forms are not proof of an independent current industrial chain. | Do not claim PE, PVC, polycarbonate, rubber and PET are equivalent. Retain configured/group uses; absent PET synthesis remains a stock limitation. |
| Mineral residues, red mud, slag, ash, spent reagents | Abundant byproducts can be deliberately low-value or waste. | Preserve legitimate recovery, construction and containment paths. No forced recycling loop or free chemical fuel is introduced. |
| Old standalone wires/heavy components/old circuit fields | A registered asset or shapeless storage conversion can survive after manufacturing migrates to metadata forms. | Compatibility-only/Optional or Unobtainable/Broken, as recorded below. Do not re-add obsolete manufacturing merely to create sinks. |

These are source/history findings, not an exhaustive claim that every changed recipe in history was accidental. The comparison ledger below retains all indexed old input references for every inventoried form, including changes that still have legitimate modern consumers.

## Native item/form census

Every native material/component field in the inventory appears below, including separate oxides, salts, gases-in-items, electronic intermediates, wastes and retained component assets. “Explicit” references are registration input/output positions, not full runtime graph proofs. The final source column catches ordinary native acquisition/consumers not expressed in those recipe signatures. Multiple forms can share a parent-material classification; conversion-only forms receive no invented independent demand. A placeholder with no meaningful source/sink stays flagged rather than counted as functional.

## Fluid/gas identity census

All declared fluid fields are included, including same-line declarations and deprecated aliases. `WATER` is the compatibility alias of `SALT_WATER`; `ACID` is legacy compatibility. `NONE` is a sentinel. Returning working solvent, circulating coolant or handling exhaust is a legitimate operational role but does not consume an unlimited mass of fresh reagent. Hot/cold, aqueous/molten and gas/liquid states are not interchangeable. Native generator/fuel/thermal consumers remain in the native-source column even when no ordinary crafting recipe consumes that field.

## Metadata and generated families

| Family | Acquisition and actual downstream use | Finding / boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Foundry ingots/plates/wires/shells/pipes/bolts/gun hardware | `Mats.orderedList` plus supported `MaterialShapes`, `OreDictManager` autogen registrations, `ItemMold`, press and assembler generators; consumers use material-specific OD keys or metadata. | Audit the actual emitted forms, not a Cartesian material×shape product. 72 q/ingot, 8 q/nugget, 9 q/fine wire, 216 q/cast plate, 432 q/welded plate, 648 q/block. IDs remain stable. New contact and ferrochrome alloys generate only ingots. |
| Old bedrock ore states | `EnumBedrockOre` and the old `ore_bedrock`, centrifuged/cleaned/separated/purified/nitrated/nitrocrystalline/deepcleaned/seared/enriched fields; generated staged separation and furnace endpoints. | Functional native state graph where the initial mining feed exists; enriched OD aliases can share ordinary ore processing. Do not count each grade as a new element. |
| New bedrock grade/type states | `ItemBedrockOreNew` has six mineral types and 26 processing grades; staged recipe generators still reference them. | Unobtainable/Broken stock initial feed when the new base remains disconnected. Internal graph entries alone do not make the acquisition chain live. No new artificial source is added in this audit. |
| Mixed waste and small isotope states | Nuclear waste enum variants, long/short/depleted/vitrified and tiny forms; reprocessing/containment and reactor outputs. | Waste treatment/containment is meaningful. Do not force all fission products into valuable components. |
| Breeding rods, RTG pellets, RBMK/PWR/Watz/ICF fuels | Each native enum drives fabrication, irradiation/burnup, spent fuel, cooling and recovery. `RodRecipes` helper registrations and reactor fuel enums are authoritative, not only direct `ModItems` references. | Optional/Specialist; fissile, fertile, heat-source, poison and clad-assembly roles are distinct. Cf/Es samples and extreme end-of-chain isotopes need not receive bulk recipes. |
| Coke/tar/ash/briquette variants | Native enum metadata plus `SolidFuel` assay and fuel-suitability tables; coking, heating, refinery, carbon and residue roles differ. | Coal coke, lignite coke and petroleum coke remain distinct. Soot/char has a carbon role; mineral ash/wood ash does not inherit it. |
| Circuit metadata | `EnumCircuitType` silicon/GaAs substrate, chips, capacitors, populated boards, control and processor states; crafting, soldering, vacuum assembly and machine consumers. | Functional. New contact metals do not replace these component counts or create chip multipliers. Old standalone circuit fields are not credited merely because they remain registered. |
| Electronic/optical crystal metadata and native items | KTP/BBO/KDP/CLBO/LBO, Ti-sapphire, LiNbO3, Ce glass, Er/Yb YAG, ZnSe, Ge and mixed dopants; chemistry → sintering/crystallization → existing optics/laser parts. | Specialist; oxide/fluoride/host crystal and dopant quantities are explicit. Whole rare-earth ingots are not generic circuit substitutes. |

## Remaining dead ends, scientific limitations and balance observations

- **Source-disconnected forms remain visible in the census.** New bedrock-feed assets, several old standalone wires/circuits, unsupported heavy-component variants and disabled novelty items are not relabeled useful on the strength of storage conversions. Repairing an entire abandoned ore-generation or fictional progression system would require a separately specified gameplay source, not an arbitrary recipe here.
- **No equal-demand target.** Rare-earth traces, radioactive poisons, refining residues, mineral ash and low-value gas coproducts can accumulate. The audit supplies no player-consumption measurements and therefore does not claim that all sources and sinks have balanced throughput. Ordinary steel/electronics/construction retain their established batch policy.
- **Expensive specialist chains.** PGM oxidation/chlorination/electrolysis, late lanthanide separation and high-purity optical crystals involve more utilities and steps than ordinary contacts. The new contact recipes are optional; this cost cannot block early copper electronics. Mass-accounted fractional return can delay the first whole product and must not be rounded into free items.
- **Chromite outputs use different existing models.** The existing Centrifuge produces two chromium powders and iron/gravel from one chromite parcel. The new chemical route uses a declared 1-kg clean oxide packet and FeCr2 recovery. Native ore-recovery gameplay counts are not a universal kilogram rule. There is no stock inverse recipe from stainless/ferrochrome into chromite/aluminium; the new route does not create a closed multiplication loop.
- **Retained historical scientific abstractions.** Manganese/selenium-only stainless, zinc/rhenium high-strength-steel shortcuts, thallium coil cores, rubidium dye quantities and some pure-metal semiconductor alternatives are not all rigorous modern engineering. They are identified rather than silently rewritten during a utilization pass. Fixing each would need a deliberate replacement chain that preserves its current legitimate demand and progression.
- **Pack overrides matter.** Enabled `hbmCrucible.json`, `hbmBlastFurnace.json` or `hbmChemplant.json` can replace stock lists. Their actual filenames are supplied by the respective loader methods. Regenerate/merge enabled old overrides to adopt new stock recipes; do not assume a default definition bypasses a configured registry. External OD aliases can change accepted feeds and should not be inferred safe from this stock audit.

## Scientific justification and source selection

These references support the material roles, not the game's batch yields or processing times:

- [USGS: Chromium statistics and information](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/chromium-statistics-and-information): chromite is refined into chromium compounds or ferrochromium; ferrochromium is a stainless-steel feed.
- [Eissa et al., Infacon XII: Aluminothermic production of extra-low-carbon ferrochromium](https://www.pyrometallurgy.co.za/InfaconXII/431-Eissa.pdf): primary experimental support for aluminothermic chromite reduction into ferrochromium. RTM's FeCr2O4 equation is a simplified clean-feed model, not a reproduction of all industrial flux/gangue operations.
- [Royal Society of Chemistry: Osmium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/76/osmium): hard contact/instrument alloys and distinction between metal and toxic volatile oxide.
- [Royal Society of Chemistry: Iridium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/77/iridium): hard corrosion-resistant alloy applications.
- [Royal Society of Chemistry: Rhodium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/45/rhodium): low-resistance, corrosion-resistant electrical contacts and specialist chemical/optical uses.
- [Royal Society of Chemistry: Ruthenium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/44/ruthenium): contact alloys and chip-resistor chemistry; oxide-anode and compound applications are distinct from pure metal.
- [Royal Society of Chemistry: Thulium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/69/thulium), [Lutetium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/71/lutetium): specialist applications do not justify mandatory bulk use. Existing isotope/optical/weapon-control roles remain limited to what RTM actually models.

## Verification record and runtime acceptance

Source checks cover unique new material/template IDs, exact item metadata, native stock registration, the chromite-to-Centrifuge dependency path, real input quantities, Foundry quantum conservation, physical mass/work ownership, and NEI's registry consumers. Regression cases in the existing `MaterialContractsTest` cover contact-alloy identity/quantity, native contact crafting (including missing conductor/wrong metadata), ferrochrome stainless input counts, native Chemical Reactor feed/product binding and paid chromite-batch reload. The registry checks use the existing dedicated-server class loader with client-only classes unavailable; this is not a Forge server launch.

Final validation on 2026-10-19: the existing Java 8 offline ForgeGradle `test build` completed successfully, including **246 automated tests, zero failures/errors and zero skipped**, followed by `jar`, `reobf`, `assemble`, `check` and `build`. The final artifact is `build/libs/RX-RNTM-[3.3_X1000].jar`. Archive inspection confirmed Java 8 class version 52 in the changed production classes, the new recipe/material identifiers and all four English labels, preserved coremod/access-transformer manifest entries, and exclusion of test classes. Targeted source and inventory/reference-coverage checks also passed. Initial test failures in the plain JVM were corrected by using the existing dedicated-server class loader and registering the new mined chromite boundary in the chemistry graph check. No Minecraft/Forge launch or visual acceptance is implied by these results.

Still required in a real stock/configured client and dedicated server: startup and configured recipe reload; NEI Recipes/Uses navigation for chromite, aluminium, alloy ingots and switch outputs; acquiring chromite from the Excavator and anvil; completing the first stainless/Centrifuge chain; reactor power-loss/full-output/chunk-unload and fractional-product persistence; hopper/item-pipe admission of both new ingot metadata; Foundry template/casting; and ordinary/specialist switch crafting and placement. Existing generic machine lifecycle tests do not replace those checks.
